items.title: Plas Johnson interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 12, 1996
items.q: he got me on fabulous recordings with Nat Cole and Frank Sinatra and Peggy Lee and Ella Mae Morse.

ctx.x: But we starved around quite a few months before getting on to something. And I met and played with Johnny Otis. Johnny Otis had his going Rhythm & Blues Revue going at the time, and I played with him a while, and I started getting calls for some rhythm & blues dates. I’m trying to remember the labels now, Modern, Aladdin — and these artists, well actually one of the artists that recorded on these labels was Charles Brown, who I first went on the road with when I was 19 years old, out in New Orleans. It was my bus…

hear you play and usually people like my playing when I play. And Johnny Otis did some records on Capitol and I had heard at Capitol via Dave Cavanaugh, who was a producer and A&R man out there, and he got me on fabulous recordings with Nat Cole and Frank Sinatra and Peggy Lee and Ella Mae Morse. I forget all the people. Capitol was a hot label at the time.
Yeah, he did some good work with Nancy Wilson.
